system_config.scenario_scale: Toy projects and undergraduate-level applications (Exclude everything listed in inputs.out_of_scope and enterprise over-engineering)
system_config.reader: A developer who has built a small project with the framework or engine in inputs.outline but has not looked at its internals

task: Write the full English article from inputs.outline. The outline fixes what the article claims; your job is to make each claim understandable through explanation, examples, and code.
article_structure: sections: Write one section per item of form.sections, in order. The section at position i develops the region at the same position, inputs.outline.regions[i], and uses that item's section_id for its anchor.

region_to_section: The section's heading is built from the region's heading. Its prose opens with the region's key_sentence as the topic sentence, reworded only as far as the flow needs. The elaboration is developed with supporting sentences and code or a text diagram, and the example is worked in where the region has one.
guidance: Each item of form.sections carries the guidance for writing that section. Follow it; it takes precedence over region_to_section where the two differ.

opening: The first section opens with two or three sentences that state the subject and the article's point of view (core_message). A later step builds the meta description from this paragraph alone, so it must stand on its own.

takeaway: Where a region has a takeaway, it is the point the section must have established by its end. Work it into the last explanatory paragraph in your own words instead of appending it as a separate closing line.
constraints: output_language: Write in English. A later step translates the finished article into Korean.

fidelity: Every claim about engine, runtime, or framework behavior must come from inputs.outline or follow directly from it. Do not add mechanisms, sections, or edge cases the outline does not contain. Details needed to make code complete (imports, annotations, method bodies) are allowed.
form_rules: Follow every item of form.rules.

section_endings: Never end a section with a standalone one-sentence paragraph that sums the section up, and never open a section's last sentence with a summing-up adverb (Ultimately, In the end, In short, In other words, Put simply). A section ends when its explanation ends. No two body sections may end with the same sentence pattern.

paragraphs: Put causal explanation in paragraphs. Link sentences with however, in contrast, therefore, or in other words where the logic turns; do not chop an explanation into a string of one-fact sentences. Use lists only for ordered steps and where a section's guidance asks for a list.
reader_questions: Where the explanation turns, you may ask the reader the question they would have at that point and answer it right away.
no_tables: Do not write summary or comparison tables. A later step adds them.

code: Use a language tag (java, python, typescript, sql, ...) only for a complete file that compiles on its own; tag excerpts as {language}-snippet (e.g., java-snippet) and diagrams as text. Every code block of 12 lines or more carries comments where it matters (why a line exists, which invariant it protects), at least one every 20 to 25 lines. Never implement anything in inputs.out_of_scope.

anchors: Start every section with <!-- sec:{id} --> using the section_id of form.sections. Place <!-- sec:code-N --> (N starting at 1) on the line immediately above each code fence, diagrams included.

allowed_markdown: paragraphs, ## and ### headings, - and 1. lists, > blockquotes, code fences, ---, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [text](url). Never use HTML tags other than the anchors, images, footnotes, or mermaid blocks.
headings: Every ## heading carries a number and a specific name (## 1. ..., ## 2. ...). Never use a bare generic heading such as 'Introduction', 'Wrapping Up', or 'Conclusion' alone.
length: Keep the prose, excluding code, within inputs.max_words words. Code fences take at most about 40% of the total characters.
honesty: Never write first-person experience, and never invent incidents, metrics, or benchmark numbers.

no_instruction_terms: Never write the project scale, audience level, or wording from these instructions (e.g., 'toy project', 'undergraduate', 'dilemma', 'key_sentence', 'core_message') into the article.
no_meta_commentary: No 'In this article', 'Let's dive in', 'To wrap up', or 'We have seen'.

output_document.title: English working title. The translation step writes the Korean headline.
output_document.body: Full English markdown body with section and code anchors. The constraints above apply to the body; the title line is the only # heading.
